tldr: Public treatment-count variation determines the order of full-record minimax precision for bounded deterministic additive outcomes over known equal containing clusters. Independently draw each cluster count from any public mean-half law and uniformly label that many treatments. With \(V=\operatorname{Var}_{\nu}K\), the risk is of order \(B^2\min\{1,D^3/(nV)\}\), with constant order at \(V=0\). A total finite regularized score attains the bound, and uniform consistency holds exactly when \(nV/D^3\to\infty\). The all-estimator converse is already forced by the smaller unknown one-to-one hidden-link subfamily. The exact fixed-law minimax constant remains open; the rule itself has the evaluated worst-case constant \(D^3/V\) at fixed \(D,\nu\) and \(B=1\).
gap: Published candidate-neighborhood scores provide fair-independent-assignment upper bounds, while baseline-assisted results and observed-exposure minimax theory do not characterize this sparse hidden-bijection record under general count laws.
fill: A total finite attaining score, a complete-label count-complement converse, and an all-law consistency equivalence determine the proposed frontier. The new burden is the universal converse rather than a new Bernoulli score.
